review_scope.method: Literal complete-group inventory only; readers and loci kept separate. Occurrence counts are bookkeeping and provide no semantic evidence.

summary.provisional_next_drafting_preference: IDEA000558 as a source-complete clause-constraint scaffold, conditionally; it is not test-ready and does not establish any target word meaning.

IDEA000554.contract: ar=HEAT and aiin=MOISTURE as Quality values; d constructs HAS(q)(subject,state), and qo negates that predicate. The target contrast is property assertion versus its negation.
IDEA000554.literal_coverage: The proposal assigns six exact forms—ar, aiin, dar, daiin, qodar, and qodaiin—with 18 complete groups per reader across the 24-locus projection (RF1b has five assigned types because its analogous qodar group is not assigned). Counts are exact-form bookkeeping only.
IDEA000554.earliest_typed_obligation: Bare ar at f85r2.1 G004 and bare aiin at f85r2.1 G030 need typed positions under the Quality-noun account. The proposal does not supply a complete owner/state grammar, so co-occurrence alone cannot refute it.
prior_equivalence_and_pressure: The existing local proposal 07_quality_complement_constructor.json already assigns dar=HOT, daiin=MOIST, and qo=NOT over the written subject/state, producing qodar/qodaiin. IDEA000554's principal change is a compositional re-factorization and a new typing obligation for bare ar/aiin, not a new HOT/MOIST plus NOT contrast.

GDT627 treats d as a measure/value head and records exact daiin in head frames as III/local measures or portions; GDT812 retains alternatives including magnitude/degree/intensity. This is a serious competing analysis of daiin, not a stop or a semantic disproof.

GDT624 already gives a productive quality grammar with hot/cold and dry/moist oppositions and binding/state operators. It is close structural precedent, although it does not parse these exact ar/aiin/d/qo forms.
IDEA000554.assessment: A potentially crisp truth-conditional contrast if participant and state are fixed, but its tested surface is close to an existing same-dossier proposal and its base forms remain under-typed. Exact form counts do not add evidence for either reading.

IDEA000555.contract: ar=HEAT, aiin=MOISTURE, and or is unary OPPOSITE over a finite table: HEAT↔COLD and MOISTURE↔DRY. Thus orar=COLD, oraiin/ or aiin=DRY, and or or aiin=MOISTURE.
IDEA000555.literal_coverage: The proposal assigns 20 exact complete groups per reader across all 24 loci. Its literal inventory includes 8 exact or groups in ZL3b and 7 each in IT2a and RF1b, plus the fused oraiin and orar groups in each reader. No altered spelling or cross-reader normalization is used.
IDEA000555.strongest_finite_obligation: A single unary operator must consume a typed QualityTerm at every exact free-or occurrence, in all three separate readings. This simultaneously constrains fused, separated, and double application under the same finite four-state table.
IDEA000555.earliest_typed_gap: At f85r2.13 G001, exact or is followed by shedy, which is unassigned and absent from the declared QualityTerm inventory. The card itself flags further unresolved or am at .15, or ain at .20, and or airol/air at .24.
IDEA000555.gap_classification: Incomplete typed contract, not a contradiction. The test would reject the fixed contract only if all permitted typed completions fail or require a forbidden repair; current unknown inputs leave it unresolved.
nearest_rivals: GDT624/623 already model hot/cold and dry/moist values in a productive quality system, without this literal or operator.

IDEA000548, an unreviewed carrier-selector proposal, uses the same or/aiin surface, including nested or or aiin, with a different typed entity/carrier contract. This is a direct surface rival, not independent support, confirmation, or an automatic scientific stop. Any later test needs a whole-block consequence that discriminates OPPOSITE from immediate-carrier selection.
IDEA000555.assessment: Of 554–556 this has the largest fixed cross-occurrence operator obligation and the earliest concrete typed gap. It still has very sparse seed values relative to the required all-occurrence grammar; do not report the 20 groups or frequent or tokens as support for the semantics.

IDEA000556.contract: ar=HEAT and aiin=MOISTURE; ot(q)(e)=SUPPLIES(e,q), requiring an explicitly written Element subject such as fire or water.
IDEA000556.literal_coverage: Exact otar and otaiin groups occur at f85r2.1 G008 and G013 in each reader; the proposal's assigned-position totals are 12 in ZL3b and 13 each in IT2a/RF1b. These counts are not semantic evidence.
IDEA000556.earliest_typed_obligation: otar at f85r2.1 G008 already needs an explicit typed Element argument; no target FIRE/WATER subject value is supplied. The analogous otod* groups are left unassigned.
IDEA000556.assessment: It offers a distinct supply/cause relation, but its literal seed is confined to two outside-locus forms and immediately depends on an unprovided subject. This is narrower than the fixed obligations in 554/555.

prior_stops_and_limits.nearest_proposal_for_554: 07_quality_complement_constructor.json is an existing same-surface HOT/MOIST plus NOT construction; the proposal should explicitly acknowledge this predecessor rather than count the refactor as a new contrast.
prior_stops_and_limits.existing_stops: GDT884's exact-source writer/STA result, F85B001's root bridge failure, and IL019's ordinal stop remain in force for the older source/text-equivalence route. They do not decide these local raw word hypotheses.
prior_stops_and_limits.other_prior_work: GDT571's OT/OL/DY labels concern abstract German outer-voice state operators and claim no changed written Voynich roots; this is not evidence for literal ot in IDEA000556.
prior_stops_and_limits.data_limit: All observations refer only to the pre-owned 24-locus safe projection; no new target data were accessed. The literal counts count full groups and do not establish parsing, meaning, independence, or confirmation.

IDEA000558_comparison.provisional_judgment: Prefer as a next drafting scaffold over another isolated quality-operator proposal, conditional on completing the source account and testing every reader separately. It makes a consequential source-level distinction—common element membership for all persons versus failure of universal treatment benefit—and fixes quantifier scope with an explicit countermodel. That is a better route to a discriminating clause contract than extending only local ar/aiin/or values. This is a drafting judgment, not a global selection or confirmation of any word.
IDEA000558_comparison.specific_consequence: N.2 is modeled as forall element forall person IS_COMPONENT_OF(element,person). The proposed ZL-only W.20 clause is NOT(forall person forall treatment IS_BENEFITED_BY(person,treatment)); this does not imply universal harm or a person-specific unsuitable item. The countermodel distinguishes it from both stronger scope rivals.
IDEA000558_comparison.coverage_and_missing_bindings: The proposal reports seven whole-form assignments, two stipulated quantifier placement licenses, two clause frames, and a four-member source-domain membership assumption for sain. The all-reader N.2 construction is present, but the W.20 benefit frame is ZL-only: IT has ar aiin and ckhedy; RF has ar aiin and ckhe@152;y, so the literal assigned ckhed[a:y] frame is unavailable in those readings under its no-alias rule. ZL's qokal shedy tail also remains unbound. Other exact or uses still require typed Domain terms, including S.13 or shedy, S.15 or am, outside .24 or airol/air, and IT W.22 or aiinog. These are incomplete bindings, not contradictions.
IDEA000558_comparison.source_completeness: The proposal itself correctly says a full account must also retain predominance/naming, the element/body-effect roster, conflict, suitable regimen, and the uncertain will/conduct qualification. Its two local derivations do not yet explain those clauses. The four-element domain assigned to sain is an explicit semantic assumption, not four target names or an independently written numeral.
IDEA000558_comparison.strongest_countercase: Only two propositions currently carry the source-level burden, and one is absent as an exact frame in IT/RF. Freely selected meanings for a sparse set of repeated forms could fit both propositions without discriminating this contract from alternatives. The more general clause/signature approach in IDEA000411 is useful as a drafting constraint but its own nearest closed grammar-complete countercases show that whole-grammar coverage alone can remain non-discriminating. Require a source-complete content table, all-target-occurrence bindings, separate reader accounts, explicit scope rivals, and a concrete outcome that changes a Voynich decision before implementation.
IDEA000558_comparison.source_validation_limit: This comparison reviews the proposal's declared source consequence and the specified existing source transcript/primary framework; it is not a fresh native review of the printed source in this task.
